attributes.body_ja:
「だらけ」は、ある物（もの）が別（べつ）の物（もの）に覆（おお）われていることや、それがいっぱいある状態（じょうたい）を表（あらわ）す接尾語（せつびご）です。

「だらけ」は、名詞（めいし）のうしろに付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。そのあとに、「〜だらけの」という形（かたち）で、別（べつ）の名詞（めいし）を修飾（しゅうしょく）することもできます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「だらけ」は、主（おも）に空（そら）に散（ち）らばる星（ほし）のように「あちこちに離（はな）れて存在（そんざい）するもの」に使（つか）われます。そのため、隙間なく覆っているものに使（つか）うと、不自然（ふしぜん）に聞（き）こえます。
attributes.body:
だらけ is a suffix that is used in Japanese to express when one thing is 'covered in', or 'filled with' another thing.

だらけ will be attached to the end of nouns, before (sometimes) being followed by the case marking particle の and a second noun. The second noun is frequently omitted if the place or thing that is 'covered in' something is obvious.

Fun Fact

だらけ is primarily used to express things that exist in a 'scattered' state (like stars in the sky). Due to this, it will not sound natural when used to describe a thing that is 'covered in' something that is not scattered in some way.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: だらけ and しか～ない are used differently and express contrasting meanings. だらけ follows nouns and expresses the idea of 'covered with' or 'full of', e.g. 泥だらけ 'covered in mud'. In contrast, しか～ない is used with a noun and negative verb to mean 'only' or 'nothing but', e.g. １００円しかない ('I have only 100 yen.'). They are similar in that both can often carry a negative or undesirable nuance.

Both indicate that something is filled with many similar elements, but the evaluation differs. だらけ means ‘full of’ with a negative or undesirable nuance, used when the items are unwanted or messy, as in ゴミだらけの部屋だ ('The room is full of trash.'). ずくめ means ‘nothing but’ with a positive or favorable nuance, used when the elements are all good or fortunate, as in いいことずくめの旅行だった ('It was a trip full of good things.').

second_relatable.meaning: Completely, Entirely, All in, Nothing but, A real streak of, Without exception, Jet

attributes.body: Both express a strong characterization, but differ in tone and focus. だらけ implies a negative excess of something undesirable, e.g. ミスだらけのレポート 'A report full of mistakes.' にほかならない expresses emphatic certainty or identity, e.g. 犯罪にほかならない 'It is nothing less than a crime.'

second_relatable.title: にほかならない
second_relatable.meaning: Nothing but, None other than, Simply

attributes.body: だらけ and 塗れ (often written in hiragana as まみれ) both describe being covered in something, but differ in nuance. だらけ suggests an overwhelming or chaotic abundance of unpleasant things, e.g. 傷だらけの手 'Hands full of cuts.' 塗れ emphasizes being soaked or stained, either physically or figuratively, e.g. 泥まみれの靴 'Mud-covered shoes' or 借金まみれの男 'A man drowning in debt.'
